question: Can the National Library of China digital object fid 412004000069 be identified as the exact Qu-family/Tieqin copy behind Zhao Wanli's 1951 'Song-printed Chunqiu Zuozhuan Zhushu' member of the 62-title donation group?
answer: No. Batch 12HK closes a necessary identity bifurcation, not a same-object identification. A public backup of NLC digital object fid 412004000069 carries NLC source provenance and catalogs 《附釋音春秋左傳注疏》六十卷 as a Liu Shugang Song-engraved ten-line copy; the observed 15-book backup run starts with book 1 containing 卷首/卷一/卷二 and book 15 containing 卷二十八/卷二十九. Separately, an official National Social Science Fund project report summarizing Zhang Lijuan's physical version research explicitly identifies an NLC-held Tieqin Tongjian Lou old-collection ten-line 《附释音春秋左传注疏》 that had been cataloged as Yuan-engraved/Ming-repaired but was re-adjudicated as a rare Yuan-engraved/Yuan-impression copy. The historical Tieqin catalog transcription supplies a closely related 60-juan entry with old Huang-family Baishong Yichan provenance and ten-line / 17-character / double-line-23-character format, while itself containing layered language about Southern-Song carving and a Yuan-time impression. These controls prove that generic title and ten-line format are insufficient for same-object collapse. The exact modern NLC shelfmark/object ID of Zhang's Tieqin-Yuan copy remains unresolved, and physical distinctness versus stale/revised catalog metadata is not formally closed. Therefore fid 412004000069 must not be equated with the Tieqin-Yuan copy or with HJ's donated member without a stable shelfmark, accession/provenance chain, ownership seal, or unique physical defect/fingerprint bridge.
